name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
role: Managed early involvement: refused to intervene at Dien Bien Phu, declined to sign the Geneva Accords, built the Diem government, and sent the first military advisers.

numbers.k: US troops in Vietnam at end of term

numbers.v: about $1.6 billion, 1955–1961, most of it military
MAAG Indochina, 342 men, inherited from Truman

decisions: The 'falling domino' press conference: the principle that would justify everything after him.
Refuses Operation Vulture, the air strike to save Dien Bien Phu, after Ridgway's estimate of what a ground war would cost and after Britain declines to join.
Does not sign the Geneva Accords; the US 'takes note' and promises not to disturb them by force.
Letter to Diem offering direct aid, bypassing the French: the start of the American client.
MAAG Vietnam takes over training of the South Vietnamese army from France — the date the US Department of Defense uses for the war's start.
Backs Diem's refusal to hold the reunification election the Accords called for.
Leaves office with about 900 advisers in country and a warning to Kennedy about Laos, not Vietnam.

advisers.note: Architect of SEATO and of the decision to build a separate South; wanted to intervene at Dien Bien Phu and was overruled.
Succeeded Dulles; Vietnam policy on autopilot.
Ex-GM; opposed a ground war in Asia on cost.
Ran the covert side, including the Saigon Military Mission.
Proposed the Dien Bien Phu strike, Vulture.
His staff study of what an Indochina ground war would need — seven divisions and more — is the reason there was not one in 1954.
'Iron Mike'; pushed for the US to take over training.
'Hanging Sam'; built the ARVN as a conventional army to fight a Korean-style invasion, which was the wrong war.
Diem's adviser and promoter; the covert operations north of the line; the model for two novels.
Recommended dropping Diem; overruled after Diem beat the sects in April 1955.
Reported Diem's decline and was ignored.
Publicly floated sending troops in April 1954; later inherited the war he had argued for.
Led the US delegation at Geneva.

text: Eisenhower: the president who said no to Dien Bien Phu, yes to Diem, and left 900 advisers and a domino theory to his successor.
